identity.name: OpenLore
identity.one_liner: Persistent architectural memory for AI coding agents using queryable codebase knowledge graphs and MCP tools.
identity.short_description: OpenLore is an open-source memory layer for AI coding agents. It turns codebases into queryable knowledge graphs with static analysis, living specs, drift detection, and MCP tools so agents can recover architectural context instead of re-discovering it every session.

positioning.why_it_matters: Coding agents lose time and quality when they lack project memory. OpenLore focuses on durable architectural memory, not just chat history or vector search.
best_for: Teams using coding agents on large or long-lived repositories
Developers who want graph-backed project memory and architecture context
Agent builders exposing codebase knowledge through MCP tools
not_for: Small scripts where repository orientation is trivial
Teams that only need document RAG rather than codebase structure

seo_article.intro: OpenLore provides persistent architectural memory for AI coding agents.
seo_article.what_it_is: It turns a codebase into a queryable knowledge graph and exposes context through MCP tools.
seo_article.why_it_matters: Coding agents need durable architecture context to avoid re-learning the same repository every session.
seo_article.how_it_works: Start by indexing a repository, inspect the generated knowledge graph and specs, then connect the memory surface to an agent workflow.

faq.question: Is OpenLore open source?
faq.answer: Yes. The GitHub repository is listed under the MIT license.

faq.question: What kind of memory does OpenLore provide?
faq.answer: It focuses on architectural and codebase memory for coding agents, including queryable code relationships and MCP tools.
